name: CA-26
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+9 district lean favors Democrats even with Brownley off the ballot
Irwin's roughly 2-to-1 fundraising edge and $366K in outside support versus none for Gallucci
Polymarket prices a Democratic win at about 94%
No public polling; open-seat uncertainty is the main residual risk
model.rationale: The district's nine-point Democratic lean, Irwin's dominant money advantage on both the candidate and outside-spending side, and market pricing near 94% all point to a comfortable Democratic hold despite the open seat. The absence of any public polling and the incumbent's retirement are the only reasons for residual uncertainty.
model.watch: A late wave of Republican outside spending or a credible poll showing Gallucci within single digits would move this race toward the competitive column.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Julia Brownley (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
California's 26th District leans Democratic by about nine points, and Julia Brownley's retirement leaves the seat open but still on favorable terrain for her party. Jacqui Irwin holds a substantial financial edge, raising more than twice as much as Sam Gallucci and banking roughly nine times his cash on hand, while outside groups have spent heavily to support her and nothing to oppose her.

Gallucci has struggled to keep financial pace, reporting just $33,681 on hand. Prediction markets price a Democratic win at about 94 percent. No public general-election polls are available, so the outlook rests on the district's partisan lean, the money gap, and market pricing. The seat remains a Safe Democratic hold, with the open-seat dynamic the main source of uncertainty.
